questions.question: Who among the following got the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for launching an effective new way to attack cancer by treating the immune system rather than the tumour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James P Allison.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **James P Allison, **an American immunologist and Nobel laureate, is a professor and chair of immunology as well as the executive director of the MD Anderson Cancer Center's immunotherapy platform.
 
• For the most lethal malignancies, his insights have produced new cancer therapies.
 
• He is best known **for helping to elucidate the mechanism behind T cell activation and for pioneering the first immune checkpoint inhibitor drug for treating cancer.**
 
• **He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for this work in 2018.**
 
• In 2014, he was awarded the Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael W Young:**

 
 
• Michael W Young is an American biologist and geneticist.
 
• He has dedicated over three decades to research studying genetically controlled patterns of sleep and wakefulness within Drosophila melanogaster.
 
• He was awarded the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine along with Jeffrey C. Hall and Michael Rosbash "for their discoveries of molecular mechanisms controlling the circadian rhythm".
 
 
 
• **Jeffrey Hall:**
 
 
• He is an American geneticist and chronobiologist. 
 
• In 2017, along with Michael W. Young and Michael Rosbash, he was awarded the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine "for their discoveries of molecular mechanisms controlling the circadian rhythm".
 
 
 
• **Michael Rosbash:**
 
 
• Michael Rosbash is an American geneticist and chronobiologist.
 
• Rosbash's research group cloned the Drosophila period gene in 1984 and proposed the Transcription Translation Negative Feedback Loop for circadian clocks in 1990.

questions.question: The Gitanjali Literary Prize is awarded in association with which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**France.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Gitanjali Literary Prize** was established in **2012 **as a** Franco-Indian literary award.** The **Mohsen Hachtroudi Foundation and CHG Earth Group** founded it (a hotel company in India).
 
• A** Gitanjali Medal, a 15-day literary sojourn, and a translation of the work** are awarded to a Francophone and an Indian author, respectively. 
 
• The French book will be edited in India by an Indian editor and the book in any of the Indian languages will be published by a French editor. 
 
• Many of the major Indian regional languages, as well as any Francophone country, are eligible. All works and genres that relate to the* year's theme are eligible for the prize.*
 
• The prize is named for the **collection of poems Gitanjali (1910) by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which Indian city was included in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network for its contribution to music in November 2017?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chennai.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **UNESCO Creative Cities Network**

 
 
• The UNESCO Creative Cities Network is a **UNESCO project that began in 2004** with the goal of** promoting cooperation among cities** that consider **creativity** a critical component of their **urban development.**
 
• The **246 cities** that now make up this network are working toward a **shared goal**: putting creativity and culture industries at the centre of their local development strategies while also engaging actively on a** global scale.**
 
 
 
• **​**As of **November 2019**, there are** five Indian cities **in **UNESCO Creative Cities Network **(UCCN) as follows:
 
 
• **Jaipur - **Crafts and Folk Arts(2015).
 
• **Varanasi - **Creative city of Music (2015).
 
• **Chennai - **Creative city of Music(2017).
 
• **Mumbai –** Film (2019).
 
• **Hyderabad –** Gastronomy (2019).
 
• **Srinagar - **Crafts and Folk Art (2021).
 
 
 
• UNESCO: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization.
 
• UNESCO's Headquarter - **Paris, France**
 
• UNESCO's Head - **Audrey Azoulay**

questions.question: Sindhi poet and writer Vasdev Mohi was selected for the Saraswati Samman, 2019. This award is given annually by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KK Birla Foundation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Saraswati Samman was instituted in 1991 by the K.K Birla Foundation.**
 
• It is an annual award for prose or poetry literary works in any of the 22 Indian languages listed in Schedule VIII of the Constitution of India.
 
• It consists of Rs 15 lakh, a citation, and a plaque.
 
• **Dr Sharan Kumar Limbale,** former head of Nashik's Yashwantrao Chavan Open University and author of 40 books to his credit, has bagged the** Saraswati Samman 2020.**
 
• **Saraswati Samman 2019** is awarded to a Sindhi writer Vasdev Mohi for his short stories collection named Chequebook.
 
• **K Siva Reddy** received the **Saraswati Award for the year 2018.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Noted poet and litterateur **Prof Ramdarash Mishra** will be awarded the prestigious **Saraswati Samman, 2021,** for his collection of poems **‘Mein to Yahan Hun’.**
 
• Instituted in 1991, Saraswati Samman is given every year to an outstanding literary work written in any Indian language by an Indian citizen and published within the last 10 yrs. 
 
• It carries a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize of ₹15 lakhs.
 
• The recipient is choosen by a selection committee, whose current head is Dr. Subhash C Kashyap, former secretary-general of the Lok Sabha Secretariat.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the French honour of ‘Chevalier dans I'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres’ (Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters) in January 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sanjana Kapoor.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Noted theatre personality **Sanjana Kapoor (daughter of famous Bollywood actor Shashi Kapoor)**, has been awarded the prestigious French honour, Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters due to her **outstanding contributions in the field of Theatre Arts.**
 
• 
 
**French Cultural Minister Franck Riester,** conferred this special distinction on **Sanjana Kapoor** in a special investiture ceremony on **January 28, 2020.**

 
 
• 
 
**Sanjana Kapoor **is the daughter of former actor **Shashi Kapoor**, who started her film career from Aparna Sen’s famous movie **"36 Chowringhee Lane" in the year 1981.**

 
 
• 
 
She also acted in films like** Hero Hiralal (1989) and Mira Nair’s Salaam Bombay (1988).**

 
 
• 
 
After some time, she decided to work fully in the field of theatre arts by acting in plays and also redeveloping the famous **Prithvi Theatre in Mumbai** which was founded by her parents.

 
 
• 
 
Some noted Indian awardees of this award include **Bharti Kher, Shahrukh Khan, Pt Hariprasad Chaurasia, Aishwarya Rai, Raghu Rai, Ebrahim Alkazi, Habib Tanveer, Upamanyu Chatterjee, Wendell Rodricks, and Aruna Vasudev, **to name a few.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ordre des Arts et des Lettres (Order of the Arts and the Letters) **is an order of France established on **2 May 1957** by **the Minister of Culture.**
 
• Its purpose is to recognize the significant contributions made in **the field of arts and literature both nationally and internationally.**
 
• The medallion is worn on a ribbon, beneath the left shoulder and is given to** not more than 200 recipients a year.**

The figure shows the image of the award.** **

questions.question: Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer who had been honoured with Padma Shri award for 2020, is associated with which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Purushottam Dadheech is a highly acclaimed Kathak dancer known for his exceptional contributions to the art form.
 
• He has been honored with the Padma Shri award in 2020 for his significant impact on Indian classical dance, especially Kathak.
 
• Purushottam Dadheech hails from Madhya Pradesh, a state with a rich cultural heritage and history in classical dance forms.
 
• He is credited with the revival and popularization of the ancient Kathak dance style in various parts of India and abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It originated from Northern India and is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• This dance form emphasizes intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Kathak has three main gharanas (schools): Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its distinct style and repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri Award**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• It is awarded to Indian citizens to recognize their distinguished contribution in various spheres of activity, including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The award is announced every year on Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh's Cultural Contributions**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known as the "Heart of India" due to its geographical location.
 
• It has a rich cultural heritage, reflected in its music, dance, and festivals.
 
• The state is home to various classical and folk dance forms, including Kathak and the tribal dance forms of the Gonds and Bhils.

questions.question: Name the album for which Pandit Ravi Shankar won the Grammy award in 1967.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Meets East.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yehudi Menuhin, **an American violinist, and** Ravi Shankar,** an Indian sitar virtuoso, collaborated on the **1967 British album West Meets East.**
 
• Following their well-received duet at the **Bath Musical Festival in June 1966,** it was recorded.
 
• Pandit Ravi Shankar won the** Grammy award in 1967** for this album.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Three Ragas:**

 
 
• **Ravi Shankar,** a Hindustani classical musician, released** Three Ragas on vinyl in 1956.**
 
• Matthew Greenwald, an** AllMusic reviewer, complimented** the CD as a **"great introduction to the medium of Indian music"** and appreciated the rendition of the raga Jog.
 
 
 
• **Concert for Bangladesh:**
 
 
• The triple live album The Concert for Bangladesh bears the **"George Harrison & Friends" credit.**
 
 
 
• **Full circle:**
 
 
• The** Doors, an American rock band**, released its eighth studio album, Full Circle, in **August 1972.**
